---
title: "Quick start"
subtitle: "From a fresh install to a finished stress test on the shipped example basin"
---

This page runs the whole pipeline once, on the example basin that ships with the
toolbox, so you can see what each stage produces before pointing it at a basin of
your own. Budget roughly an hour of machine time.

If the toolbox is not installed yet, do that first: [Setup guide](../install.md).

::: {.callout-important}
## Both install steps, not just the first

```bash
pixi install       # Python stack, R toolchain, Snakemake, Graphviz
pixi run install   # + the weathergenr weather generator (R) and the Julia environment
```

`pixi install` alone is **not** enough to run the stress test: the weather
generator is installed from GitHub by the second command, and a run without it
fails an hour in with `there is no package called 'weathergenr'`. Julia itself
is deliberately outside the pixi environment — it is managed by juliaup and must
already be on your `PATH`.
:::

## The shape of a run

Five workflows share one project configuration set:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    wf0["wf0 · analyze_climate<br/>optional historical analysis"]
    wf1["wf1 · build_model<br/>Wflow-SBM + historical run"] --> wf4
    wf3["wf3 · generate_scenarios<br/>ready collection"] --> wf4
    wf4["wf4 · simulate_system<br/>responses and metrics"]
    wf2["wf2 · analyze_projections<br/>terminal plausibility overlay"]
```

Generation and model construction are independent prerequisites of simulation.
**wf0 is optional** for the pipeline: it
produces the region, vector layers and climate store that wf1 also declares, so
running it first simply means those already exist when the build asks. Run it
*alone* when your question is which forcing dataset to use. **wf2 never drives a
run** — its change factors situate the perturbation grid in projection space,
nothing more.

## Pick a configuration

Two configurations ship with the toolbox, both under `test_case/`, both
describing the same basin:

| Config | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `test_case/project_config_rapid.yml` | **the default.** Anything you want to watch *execute* — a first run, a rule you edited, a smoke test |
| `test_case/project_config_baseline.yml` | runs whose *numbers* you will quote or compare |

Rapid is cheap, not narrow: it keeps the historical baseline scenario and two
CMIP6 models, so no code path is skipped — it just runs fewer years and fewer
members. Start there.

## Run it

From the repository root, inside the pixi environment:

```bash
pixi shell

python scripts/run_workflows.py --config test_case/project_config_rapid.yml --project-dir test_case/test_rapid --cores 3
```

The wrapper runs whichever workflows the config enables, in order. Set only
`generate_scenarios.enabled: true` to run WF3 alone.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Look before you leap

`--dry-run` (`-n`) lists what *would* execute without running anything. It is
the cheapest way to confirm the workflow can resolve its inputs, and it costs
seconds:

```bash
snakemake all -c 3 -s build_model.smk --configfile test_case/project_config_rapid.yml --dry-run
```
:::

## What you get

Everything lands under the `project_dir` named in the config —
`test_case/test_rapid` for the rapid config:

```
test_case/test_rapid/
  data/spatial/         basin, subbasins, rivers, gauge locations, and their plots
  data/climate/         the historical climate store, and the CMIP6 slices
  models/hydrology/     the Wflow-SBM model, its forcing, its run, its evaluation
  scenarios/requests/   exact generation requests
  scenarios/collections/ durable forcing and portable preparation inputs
  experiments/<name>/   one simulation identity, native responses and metric sets
  logs/                 one log per workflow
  benchmarks/           per-rule timings
  config/runs/          what each run was configured with (see Reading the outputs)
```

The stress test's payoff is in `experiments/<name>/results/metric_sets/`: the hydrological
indicators computed for every temperature × precipitation combination, which
form the response surface.

## When something goes wrong

- **"Directory cannot be locked"** — a previous run crashed. Clear it:
  `snakemake --unlock -s <workflow>.smk --configfile <config>`.
- **`there is no package called 'weathergenr'`** — the second install step was
  skipped; run `pixi run install`.
- **Julia not found** — Julia is deliberately not in the pixi environment. It is
  managed by juliaup and must be on your `PATH`; see the
  [Setup guide](../install.md).
